- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to avoid undershooting.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; reduce forecast by 3–5% in the immediate follow-up period.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.5) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates near-term upside; cap forecast at +3% above recent 7-day average.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods when sentiment is neutral (0.1–0.3); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for lagged reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-cycle corrections; if sentiment turns negative after a peak, add 1–2% downward bias in final 5–7 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.1–0.2), model tends to ignore downward momentum; apply a 1–3% downward adjustment to avoid false optimism.
